title: Compliance Culture: Masterclass and Capstone
summary: Brings the series together by examining how compliance culture shows itself in behaviour, incentives and tone from the top, and applies the full series to an integrated firm case study.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the series together by examining how compliance culture shows itself in behaviour, incentives and tone from the top, and applies the full series to an integrated firm case study.
Learning Objectives: Assess indicators of a firm's compliance culture
Integrate findings across compliance areas into an overall view
Formulate proportionate supervisory responses and follow-up
Syllabus: Tone from the top and the middle: culture in practice
Incentives, speaking up and breach reporting as cultural indicators
From individual weaknesses to an overall compliance risk assessment
Workshop: integrated firm case study and supervisory action plan
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for assessing firms' compliance and control arrangements
AML/CFT, conduct and governance specialists who review firms' policies, procedures and testing
Newer supervisors and staff moving into supervision from compliance roles in industry
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision or of compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. Each masterclass is self-contained, so no prior attendance is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
